title: Why You Can't Trust Volatility Anymore
speaker: tastylive hosts

macro_themes.view: The 40-50 year era of structurally falling rates and low inflation is over, so historical volatility analogs and the structural risk-on bid can't be trusted.
CoreWeave may be the first casualty of the AI boom, like early subprime lenders before Bear Stearns; there is never one cockroach.

calls.reason: Down another 13.6%; bonds imply >63% default probability; host says fade the call buyers chasing a bounce and frames it as possibly the first AI casualty.
Feels like a flush, not a buy-the-dip, with a possible multi-percent drop within a week or two as VIX jumped to 20.
calls.quote: when we say flush, we mean not a buy the dip opportunity. We mean a worth multitudes of percentage points down within a week or two.

notes: Multiple hosts in crosstalk; attribution of quotes uncertain. VIX ~20 mention with a hint at selling premium was not recorded as a VIX call. Recording day is likely mid-week (VIX spike, CRWV -13.6%), earlier than listing date.
